reasons: Both give the same correct core answer with one brief lease caveat and no disclaimer, and both run slightly over 150 words (about 162 vs 170). B adds the claim that missing the 21-day deadline may forfeit the landlord's right to keep anything, which overstates California law (Granberry v. Islay Investments holds the landlord can still prove damages). A instead adds the accurate useful-life proration point and is slightly tighter.

B: Implies a landlord who misses the 21-day itemization deadline may lose the right to keep any deduction; under Granberry v. Islay Investments the landlord can still recover proven damages, though missing it can support a bad-faith penalty.
